summary: Roundup of Collingwood's 2023 AFL premiership aftermath. Coach Craig McRae revealed he wore "44 sons" under his collar, part of a legacy exercise in which every player chose words to be remembered by. The note also covers Oleg Markov's path from the AFL scrapheap, Jeremy Howe's rib injury, Brayden Maynard's relief after the Brayshaw incident, and players who missed the grand final.
one_line: After Collingwood's four-point grand final win, McRae revealed his "44 sons" collar message amid stories of Markov, Howe, Maynard and those who missed out.
key_facts: Craig McRae wore the message "44 sons" under the collar of his shirt in the grand final, signifying how he felt about each player in the 2023 squad.
McRae has three daughters and no son; his wife Gabrielle gave birth to daughter Maggie at 7.45am on grand final morning at St Vincent's Hospital.
Each Collingwood player wrote words under his jumper collar describing the legacy he wanted to leave as a person and player in 2023.
Collingwood won the grand final by four points over Brisbane, the club's 16th premiership.
Dan McStay, who joined from the Lions as an unrestricted free agent, may need up to eight weeks to recover from a high-grade medial collateral ligament strain suffered in the preliminary final.
John Noble played every home-and-away game but was dropped for the qualifying final against Melbourne and never returned to the team.
Oleg Markov, 27, was delisted by Gold Coast, played 23 games for Richmond, trialled with Carlton, then joined Collingwood after Charlie Dean re-fractured his right foot, opening a list spot.
Markov missed out on all three Richmond flags (2017, 2019 and 2020) despite playing senior games in each of those years.
Markov's father Dmitri won the men's pole vault at the 2001 world championships.
Jeremy Howe played out the grand final with badly bruised ribs after a late hit from Brisbane's Charlie Cameron; earlier in the season he broke his arm in six places in round one.
Brayden Maynard faced a three-match ban threat after his collision with Melbourne's Angus Brayshaw before beating the charge at the tribunal.
Maynard said the Magpies had to lap up the premiership but warned it was just the beginning as they bid to become a dynasty.
Nathan Murphy took no further part in the grand final after being concussed in a clash with Brisbane's Linc McCarthy.
Collingwood president Jeff Browne, who had a health scare on the eve of the finals, said the win was "the ultimate satisfaction" and honoured the club's history.
